name: pselect
synopsis: int pselect(int nfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict readfds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict writefds, fd_set *_Nullable restrict exceptfds, const struct timespec *_Nullable restrict timeout, const sigset_t *_Nullable restrict sigmask);
description: pselect() is a variant of select() that allows a program to monitor multiple file descriptors for I/O readiness while atomically setting a signal mask to prevent race conditions. It waits until one or more descriptors become ready for operations like reading or writing, with an optional timeout.

parameters.name: nfds
parameters.description: The highest-numbered file descriptor in any of the sets plus one.

parameters.name: readfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for readability.

parameters.name: writefds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for writability.

parameters.name: exceptfds
parameters.description: Set of file descriptors to monitor for exceptional conditions.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout period for the operation, or NULL for no timeout.

parameters.name: sigmask
parameters.description: Signal mask to atomically set during the call, or NULL to leave unchanged.

return_value.success: Returns the number of file descriptors ready for I/O in the sets, or zero if the timeout expired
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and sets errno; the file descriptor sets are unmodified

errors.description: An invalid file descriptor was given in one of the sets.
nfds is negative or exceeds the RLIMIT_NOFILE resource limit, or timeout is invalid.
Unable to allocate memory for internal tables.

bugs: The fd_set implementation has a fixed limit of FD_SETSIZE (1024), making it unsuitable for monitoring descriptors beyond this; select() and pselect() may report spurious readiness on sockets; the glibc emulation of pselect() in older versions was vulnerable to race conditions, though modern versions use the kernel system call; select() modifies timeout on interruption, which is a design flaw.
